source_name: iROZHLAS / Czech Radio – data reporting on municipalities losing branches and ATMs
why_relevant: Public-service broadcaster data journalism mapping municipalities without bank branches or ATMs and the alternatives banks offer; typically sourced from bank questionnaires, so it surfaces numbers not otherwise published.

source_name: Aktuálně.cz – Euronet rural ATM rollout and municipal subsidy reporting
why_relevant: Documents the IAD-to-municipality commercial model (monthly fee paid by the obec to host an ATM) and estate splits between tourist and rural locations — quantified evidence for how the non-bank ATM estate is financed.

source_name: COOP / retail cooperative network – cash-back at checkout provider
why_relevant: Reported to handle roughly two-thirds of Czech cash-back withdrawals thanks to its rural store density; its own communications are the best actor-level source on cash-at-POS as a branch/ATM substitute.

source_name: Česká justice – legislative tracking of the constitutional right to pay in cash
why_relevant: Follows the repeated parliamentary/Senate attempts to constitutionalise cash payment, the government's and ČNB's positions, and comparisons with SK/HU/SI/CH. Cash-acceptance politics is the main generator of quantified public evidence on cash usage in this cell.

source_name: Parlament ČR – sněmovní/senátní tisky on cash-payment guarantees
why_relevant: Primary documents (bill texts, explanatory memoranda, government and ČNB opinions) behind the cash-acceptance debate; explanatory memoranda usually contain the only official quantification of cash usage and access used in policy.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (e-commerce association, studies & surveys)
why_relevant: The Czech e-commerce trade association; publishes the recurring E-commerce Study Czech Republic and consumer surveys that include payment-method share (card-in-advance, dobirka/COD split, wallets, BNPL). This is the canonical acceptance-side view of online payment mix that ChNB/banking statistics do not break out.

source_name: APEK data portal (data.apek.cz)
why_relevant: Dedicated data portal launched by APEK (~2025) presenting Czech e-commerce indicators, reportedly including payment-method breakdowns over time. A structured, repeatable numeric source rather than one-off PR numbers.

source_name: Ceska-ecommerce.cz – Shoptet / Zbozi.cz real-time Czech e-commerce portal
why_relevant: Operated by Shoptet (platform behind roughly a quarter of Czech e-shops) with Zbozi.cz; tracks in near-real time the number of online merchants, turnover, best-sellers and related e-commerce quantities. Platform-derived acceptance data with far higher frequency than survey-based sources.

source_name: Shoptet press releases & Shoptet Blog (payment methods / gateways)
why_relevant: Largest Czech e-shop platform; its press room and blog publish aggregate platform statistics and recurring 'payment methods and payment gateways in year X' overviews that describe the acceptance mix available and used across thousands of merchants.

source_name: Shoptet Pay – gateway product & supported payment methods
why_relevant: Shoptet's own payment gateway. Its supported-methods pages and product announcements are a direct read on which acceptance methods (cards, wallets, A2A/instant transfer, BNPL) are being pushed into the long tail of Czech e-shops.

source_name: GoPay blog / payment methods & technology category
why_relevant: One of the largest CZ/SK gateways; publishes gateway comparisons, method-mix commentary and occasional share statistics (e.g. card active in >90% of e-shops). Useful for method adoption and competitive landscape at the acceptance layer.

source_name: Comgate – blog and 'Napsali o nás' (press clippings)
why_relevant: Major Czech gateway/PSP that discloses concrete gateway-level method shares in its own communications — e.g. QR payments up to ~20% of gateway transactions, bank transfer ~20%, Air Bank 'Cvak' approaching ~10% among Air Bank clients. Rare quantitative A2A/QR evidence unavailable from banking statistics.

source_name: ThePay (payment gateway) – company communications and trade-press coverage
why_relevant: Top-3 Czech e-commerce gateway by its own account (~4,000 merchants; ~CZK 7bn processed in a reported year) and a vocal source on wallet trends (Apple Pay). Gateway-level volume disclosures are a proxy for online acceptance growth.

source_name: PayU Czech Republic (incl. Twisto BNPL integration pages)
why_relevant: International PSP with a dedicated Czech operation; product and partner pages document which local methods (cards, bank transfers, BNPL via Twisto) are offered to Czech merchants, and PayU/Prosus group reporting occasionally carries regional volume commentary.

source_name: Besteron (Pay Solutions a.s.) – CZ/SK/PL/SI gateway
why_relevant: Slovak-origin gateway active in the Czech market; relevant for cross-border CZ/SK acceptance comparison (notably the CZ instant-transfer vs SK cash-on-delivery divergence). Named in the coverage cell brief.

source_name: Skip Pay (Č SOB group BNPL) – merchant/gateway comparison and product pages
why_relevant: Bank-owned Czech BNPL/deferred-payment provider on the acceptance side; publishes merchant-facing gateway comparisons and BNPL adoption messaging. Key for tracking BNPL share of Czech e-commerce baskets.

source_name: Twisto Payments – Czech BNPL pioneer
why_relevant: The most-cited Czech BNPL brand (pay-later, pay-in-3), distributed via PayU and directly to merchants. Company communications and third-party profiles are the main handle on BNPL penetration of Czech e-commerce (~5-7% of online payment volume per secondary sources).

source_name: Heureka Group press centre – 'Heureka eCommerce Insider' quarterly series
source_subtype: corporate press room / recurring index series
why_relevant: The de-facto quarterly benchmark for Czech e-commerce turnover, growth and average order value (e.g. CZK 194bn total 2024; AOV ~CZK 1,889 in H1 2026), derived from comparison-shopping traffic and merchant data. Basket-statistics backbone for the acceptance side.

source_name: SOCR ČR – Svaz obchodu a cestovního ruchu ČR (retail & tourism association)
why_relevant: The retail merchants' lobby, which publishes member surveys on the merchant cost of card acceptance (e.g. seven largest chains paying ~CZK 1.4bn in card fees in 2022) and lobbies on interchange/alternative payments. Uniquely gives the merchant-cost and merchant-motivation view of acceptance economics.

source_name: Mastercard Czech Republic consumer payment surveys (iResearch / G82 fieldwork) via press coverage
why_relevant: Recurring representative Czech consumer surveys on contactless, mobile and digital-wallet payment behaviour (e.g. 61% using mobile contactless; ~86% of issued cards contactless; Jan-2026 wave n=1,212 by agency G82). Scheme-side demand data that complements gateway supply-side data.

source_name: Retail News (retailnews.cz)
why_relevant: Czech retail trade magazine that reliably republishes Heureka Insider quarters, Mastercard surveys, APEK findings and retailer payment stories — an efficient single feed for discovering new acceptance-side data releases and their originators.

source_name: Ecommerce Bridge CZ (ecommercebridge.cz)
why_relevant: Czech e-commerce professional media covering payment trends, gateway selection, A2A/instant payments and PSP interviews. A good snowball hub for identifying new gateways, BNPL entrants and the practitioners who hold acceptance data.

source_name: e-shop.report – Czech e-commerce trends & analytics
why_relevant: Aggregator of Czech e-shop counts, category structure and trend analytics; useful denominator data (how many active e-shops, what size) against which gateway and payment-method penetration claims can be normalised.

source_name: Datalook.cz – Shoptet platform/company data report
why_relevant: Third-party company/market data profiles that can corroborate platform scale claims (merchant counts, financials) used to weight Shoptet-derived acceptance statistics.

source_name: Dotykačka – POS/cash-register vendor (retail & hospitality)
why_relevant: Large Czech POS vendor bundling card acceptance and pricing partly by card turnover; its reporting products and occasional PR aggregate physical-retail/gastro transaction and card-share data — the offline counterpart to gateway data, and a route to ATM/POS-adjacent acceptance intelligence.

source_name: Storyous (Solitea/Saltpay group) – POS analytics for gastro/retail
why_relevant: POS vendor with an explicit data/analytics product covering turnover, tips and shift-level sales for Czech hospitality and small retail; a potential source of aggregate card-vs-cash mix at the physical point of acceptance.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – e-shop payment gateway (acquirer/bank merchant side) and analyst e-commerce papers
source_subtype: bank acquirer product page + bank research
why_relevant: Bank acquirer offering an e-shop gateway; the bank's analytics team also publishes e-commerce trend papers. Bridges the banking-centric and acceptance-centric views and can carry merchant-acceptance volume commentary.

source_name: Czech gateway comparison round-ups (Upgates, FastCentrik, WebhostingCentrum, FEO, Eshop-rychle)
why_relevant: Annually refreshed comparisons of 10-15+ Czech/Slovak gateways with fees, supported methods and settlement terms. The fastest way to maintain a complete, current actor map of the CZ acceptance layer, including small and new entrants.
